verdict.rationale: Braintrust explicitly documents scoring outputs "with LLMs, code, or humans" (docs-68). Scorers are first-class, authorable objects: you can iterate on them in playgrounds, manage them via the API, author them through MCP, and run them in experiments or as online scoring on production traces. missing for 10: detailed documentation of LLM-judge configuration (judge model, prompt templates, score mappings), an LLM-judge code example (the GitHub example uses only a Levenshtein scorer), and independent hands-on corroboration.
